summary: CeDeFi yield platform that closed in December 2022 after sustained DeFi portfolio losses, heavy withdrawals during the Celsius and FTX crises, and a disclosed deficit between customer liabilities and remaining assets.
what_happened: Midas Investments operated centralized fixed-yield accounts backed by platform-managed CeDeFi and DeFi strategies. Its closure explanation described a roughly $50 million DeFi portfolio loss during spring 2022 and further pressure when users withdrew more than 60% of assets after the Celsius and FTX failures. On 27 December 2022 Midas stopped ordinary platform activity, recalculated customer balances, applied deductions to several major asset balances and historical rewards, and announced token-based compensation while winding down the existing business.
uncertainty_notes: The 2018 launch date remains approximate. Midas was not modeled as a court-supervised bankruptcy, and the announced balance adjustment and token compensation do not establish one final market-value recovery percentage for every customer.
